member.name: T:ModLib.AutoTest.AutoTestRunner
member.summary: In-game test runner of a mod, driven by scripts/game/run-autotest.ps1 of ModLib (shared by the mods). Loaded only when <mod cache>\autotest\request.json exists (never for normal players). Phases: title screen scenarios -> load the save (automatically or by the tester) -> game scenarios -> optional battle watching. Results and screenshots are written to the request OutDir. The runner never saves the game; use a throwaway test save anyway. A mod declares its runner as a subclass with a Cache attribute, e.g. [Cache("AutoTestEvent", CacheType = CacheAttribute.CType.Global, WorkOn = CacheAttribute.WType.All)] public class AutoTestEvent : AutoTestRunner { ... }, and its scenarios as IScenarioDefinition classes of its assembly. The hooks (ModVersion, OnRequestLoaded, OnNewCharacterRequested, CaptureModState / RestoreModState) add what is specific to the mod.

Games that stay open (run-autotest-parallel.ps1, AutoTestRequest.KeepAlive): once its scenarios are done the game waits in the save (phase Idle) for the next request - a request.json with another RunId written by run-autotest.ps1 -Attach - and runs it at once, without a restart. Every game scenario starts from the player state recorded when the save was loaded (the baseline: grade, exp, money, lifespan, age, place, HP / MP / SP, bag, the data of the mod: CaptureModState / RestoreModState), then its own Scenario.Precondition.

member.name: T:ModLib.Helper.FileWriteQueue
member.summary:
Writes text files on a worker thread, skipping a file whose content did not change since the last write.
The caller serializes on its own thread (game objects are not safe to read from another thread) and passes the text: only the disk write runs on the worker. A file is skipped when the text equals the one last written to it and the file on disk is still the one written (same size and time: a file changed or deleted by someone else is written again).
Safety: each file is written to "<file>.tmp" and then replaces the file, so a failed or interrupted write never leaves a half-written file. A failed write is reported (OnError) and forgotten, so the next save writes it again. Only the newest text of a file waits in the queue. The worker is a foreground thread: the process does not exit before the queue is written. Flush waits for the queue (before reading the files again).

member.name: T:ModLib.Helper.AttributeTargetHelper`1
member.summary: Helps in discovery of the target of an Attribute
member.remarks:
The .NET framework does not provide navigation from attributes back to their targets, principally for the reason that in typical usage scenarios for attributes, the attribute is discovered by a routine which already has a reference to a member type.
There are, however, bona-fide cases where an attribute needs to detect it's target - an example is a localizable sub-class of the DescriptionAttribute. In order for the DescriptionAttribute to return a localized string, it requires a resource key and, ideally, a type reference as the base-key for the ResourceManager. A DescriptionAttribute could not provide this information without a reference to it's target type.
Note to callers:
Your Attribute-derived class must implement Equals and GetHashCode, otherwise a run-time exception will occur, since this class creates a dictionary of attributes in order to speed up target lookups.

member.summary: Sends the exceptions logged by DebugHelper.WriteLine(Exception) to BugSplat, to the database of the mod where the error happened, only when the player allowed it (ModTitleEvent.CrashReportConsent). Each mod using ModLib sets its own database in its ModConf/crash_reports.json (no file: its errors are not sent): { "Database": "my-bugsplat-db", "ModName": "My mod", "LogLines": 200 } The mod of an error: the first MOD_<modId> assembly in the stack of the exception (innermost first), then in the stack of the code that logged it.
